question: What is the initial waiting period before any claim can be made?
expected_answer: 30 days from the first policy start for any illness; accident claims are excepted; it does not apply if you have had continuous coverage for more than 12 months
app_answer:
According to Niva Bupa, the initial waiting period (Excl03) is 30 days for all illnesses from the first policy commencement date [19, 21]. During this initial 30-day period, expenses related to the treatment of any illness are excluded, except for claims arising due to an accident [19, 21]. This initial waiting period does not apply in the case of continuous renewal or accidents [21], or if the insured person has continuous coverage for more than twelve months [19]. 

This is information from the documents, not insurance or legal advice. Please confirm with your insurer.

question: Is there a room rent limit?
expected_answer: Yes if opted; a limit per day applies as shown in the Policy Schedule and if the room rent is higher the payout is reduced proportionately
app_answer:
According to the Go Digit Supreme Care policy, hospital accommodation is subject to a limit per day as opted by you and mentioned in your Policy Schedule or Certificate of Insurance [2]. If the room rent rate exceeds your chosen limit during hospitalization, the insurer's liability will be restricted to the proportion that your opted limit bears to the actual room rent rate [2]. This proportionate restriction applies to room charges, except for the cost of medicines and consumables [2]. However, this condition can be specifically waived off if mentioned in your Policy Schedule or Certificate of Insurance [2]. 

This is information from the documents, not insurance or legal advice. Please confirm with your insurer.

question: Which documents are needed to file a reimbursement claim?
expected_answer: Signed claim form; NEFT details or cancelled cheque; ID proof (KYC); address proof if applicable; and for hospitalization: discharge summary; medical records; original hospital bills and bill break-up; pharmacy bills; prescriptions; investigation reports
app_answer:
According to Go Digit, for a Hospitalization Claim, you need a discharge summary, medical records (with optional documents like indoor case papers, OT notes, and PAC notes asked on a need basis), original hospital main bill, original hospital bill break up, original pharmacy bills, and prescriptions for medicines purchased and investigations done outside the hospital [2]. You also need consultation papers, investigation reports, digital images or CDs of investigation procedures if required, and an MLC or FIR report if applicable [2]. Additional documents that may be needed depending on the case include an original invoice or sticker, post-mortem report, disability certificate, attending physician certificate, ante-natal record, birth discharge summary, death certificate, or any other documents on a case-to-case basis [2]. 

This is information from the documents, not insurance or legal advice. Please confirm with your insurer.

question: What happens if a hospital stay lasts more than 7 days and Niva Bupa is not informed?
expected_answer: An extra 10% co-payment is applied on the final admissible amount (the limit is 9 days for road traffic accidents)
app_answer:

This co-payment applies if the treatment is taken for an illness or surgery other than what was informed earlier, if the treatment is taken outside the recommended network provider, or if Niva Bupa is not informed within 24 hours of admission [14]. The specific rules for stays lasting more than 7 days are not in the policy wording, it is in your Policy Schedule [1].

question: How do the two policies handle room rent limits?
expected_answer: Niva Bupa: a room above the eligible category in the Policy Schedule means a pro-rated payout and variants have room category co-payments; Digit: a daily limit as opted in the Policy Schedule and a proportionate reduction if it is exceeded
app_answer:
For Niva Bupa (ReAssure 3.0), if you choose a room higher than your eligible category, they pay only a pro-rated portion of total Associated Medical Expenses based on the formula: (Eligible Room Rent limit / Room Rent actually incurred) * total Associated Medical Expenses [2]. For Go Digit (Digit Supreme Care), if your room rent rate exceeds your opted limit, their liability is restricted in the same proportion as the admissible rate per day limit bears to the actual rate per day, except for medicines and consumables [14, 17, 20].

This is information from the documents, not insurance or legal advice. Please confirm with your insurer.

question: How do the two policies treat the waiting period for pre-existing diseases?
expected_answer: Niva Bupa: 36 months of continuous coverage; Digit: the number of months opted and shown in the Policy Schedule; both reduce it for prior continuous coverage (portability)
app_answer:
For Niva Bupa (ReAssure 3.0), expenses for pre-existing diseases and their direct complications are excluded until the expiry of 36 months of continuous coverage after the first policy starts [1]. 
For Go Digit (Digit Supreme Care), pre-existing disease expenses are excluded until the expiry of a number of months opted by you and specified in your Policy Schedule, following continuous coverage from the first policy's inception [11]. 
For both insurers, if you increase your sum insured, the waiting period applies afresh to the increased amount [1, 11]. 
Additionally, both insurers state that if you are continuously covered without a break under IRDAI portability norms, the waiting period is reduced by your prior coverage [1, 11]. 
For Niva Bupa, coverage after 36 months also requires the disease to be declared at application and accepted [1]. 
For Go Digit, coverage after the waiting period is likewise subject to the pre-existing disease being declared at application and accepted by the insurer [11].

This is information from the documents, not insurance or legal advice. Please confirm with your insurer.
